facts.text: It has been getting worse; it's worse now than when it began.
It began two years after I started vismodegib, about 8 years ago, as loose stools two or three times a day.
I take loperamide, up to 5 doses a day.
I've taken vismodegib 150 mg every day for 10 years.
I've taken it without any interruptions, even after the loose stools started.
I have basal cell carcinoma that is locally advanced and has spread (metastatic).
I've had colonoscopies before: one after 5 years of this treatment and one after 9 years.
My sense of taste has changed.

facts.item: hair, taste or muscle symptoms linked to diarrhea episodes
facts.text: The hair loss, taste change and muscle spasms don't come and go with my diarrhea episodes.
I haven't had any other general symptoms.

gold.reasoning: 1. Broad differential diagnosis including infection, ischemia, graft-versus-host disease, IBD, and drug effects — “The nonspecific histologic findings in this case yield a broad differential diagnosis of infectious causes (including viral infections), ischemia, graft-versus-host disease, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and medication/drug effects.” 2. Epithelial apoptosis suggests a medication-related etiology (also seen in graft-versus-host disease and viral infections) — “the presence of epithelial apoptosis raises the likelihood of a medication-related etiology because epithelial apoptosis is characteristically associated with medication effects, graft-versus-host disease, and viral infections.” 3. Infectious etiologies excluded by negative molecular and immunohistochemical studies — “the result of polymerase chain reaction–based testing for infectious etiologies (including bacterial and viral entities) was negative. A cytomegalovirus stain performed on the tissue was also negative.” 4. IBD considered but less likely given absence of pronounced active inflammation and presence of epithelial apoptosis — “IBD typically presents with a more pronounced active inflammatory infiltrate and lack of epithelial apoptosis.” 5. Medication effect deemed most likely based on clinicopathologic correlation — “These findings led us to conclude that a medication/drug effect was the most likely etiology.”

f002: The source grades the diarrhea (CTCAE grade 1 at onset, grade 2 now); the grades are clinician scoring and are rendered as 'worse now than when it began' without inventing stool counts.
f003: 'About 8 years ago' is arithmetic: onset two years into ten years of vismodegib.
f010: The patient is not said to have been told the earlier colonoscopy results, so only the fact that they were done is a patient fact; the results are findings with time.

notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with worsening watery diarrhea after 10 years of daily vismodegib (s001, s004–s008), with the repeat colonoscopy and biopsies of that workup (s009–s012).
The earlier colonoscopies and random biopsies (s003) are findings with time; the repeat colonoscopy is the current one.
Gold aliases include drug-induced colitis/ileocolitis forms: the biopsies show the drug-related ileocolitis that causes the diarrhea, so these name the same entity more specifically.
